title: `echo "a b`<newline>`$HO`: zsh offers nothing inside the unterminated quote, zshrs lists HOME/HOST

observed.detail: diverges at step #1 ('tab'); first diff row 2 col 0; 2 row(s) differ
observed.notes: Both shells answer the Enter with PS2 — the buffer is deliberately incomplete at the newline, so nothing executes and the completion fires inside the continuation. The single-line control below completes the same word with the newline removed and PASSES, which is what makes the CONTINUATION the variable rather than the word. No zstyle at all on either side (`--no-zstyle`), so this is the engine on defaults: the word is inside a double-quoted string that opened on the previous physical line, and only zshrs treats `$HO` there as a completable parameter.

controls.note: `echo "a b $HO` on one line — same unterminated quote, no newline: PASSES.

zshrs_binary.kind: debug build under target/ (NOT the Homebrew-installed zshrs)

zsh_binary.note: Homebrew zsh 5.9.2, which is what `zsh` on PATH resolves to here; /bin/zsh is an older build and is NOT what any harness runs.

confirmed.note: the three sibling harnesses were being edited by other agents while this was confirmed, and `target/` was deleted mid-session (disk full) taking every round-3 reproducer with it; every cell below was re-run against the rebuilt binary identified above.
